sections.h2: What does the Eaton County Register of Deeds actually do?
sections.html:
Eaton County's register keeps the county's land title file: deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and any other paper that touches real estate between Charlotte, Grand Ledge, Eaton Rapids and the townships around them. Each filing is checked against Michigan's recording rules and then stored as a digital image.

Staff will not draft a deed or fill one in. The county's own page says the content and intent of a document are the responsibility of whoever prepared it, and anyone with a legal question should see an attorney. A seller who needs a deed written should start with a title company or real estate lawyer and bring the signed original afterward.

The counter keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 4:30 and shuts between noon and 1:00 every day. Courthouse holidays interrupt that schedule, as the notice about Veterans Day on the register's page shows. Anything sent by mail should include a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, because the office requires one before it sends documents back.

sections.h2: What fees does Eaton County charge at the recording counter?
sections.html:
The standard charge is $30 for each deed, mortgage, lis pendens or certified copy of a real estate paper. Extras are itemized on the county's fees page.

Charges at the Eaton County register, as posted by the county
ItemCharge
Recording a deed, mortgage or similar paper$30
Every added instrument assigned or discharged in the same document$3 each
Tax certificate covering up to 25 descriptions$5
Every description after the 25th$0.20
Plain copy of a land record$1 a page
Copy of a recorded plat$2 a page
Certifying a recorded document$1 a page plus $5 for the seal

Certification is not sold through the website, so ask at the counter or by mail.

sections.h2: Which Eaton County deeds need a tax certificate first?
sections.html:
Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of land contracts must arrive with a certificate from the county treasurer's office. The county points to MCL 211.135, and that statute asks for confirmation that no tax liens or tax titles sit on the parcel and that taxes were settled for the five years leading up to the instrument.

The same law carves out quitclaim deeds and other conveyances without warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds and state tax deeds. A closer ordinarily orders the certificate during escrow, so sellers rarely chase it personally.

  • A treasurer's tax certificate attached to any warranty deed or land contract.
  • Total value written on the deed, or a valuation affidavit stapled to it.
  • Return postage and an addressed envelope for mailed packages.
  • $30 to record, plus the $5 certificate charge when one applies.

Anything incomplete goes back to the sender, and that can push a closing by several days. If the parcel carries unpaid taxes, the treasurer will not issue a clean certificate until those are cleared.

sections.h2: What transfer tax comes due on an Eaton County sale?
sections.html:
Two levies ride on the deed. The state charges $3.75 for each $500 of value (MCL 207.525). The county charges 55 cents for each $500, the rate set for counties with fewer than two million people (MCL 207.504). Both count the whole value and round up to the next $500 step.

The law places both on the seller (MCL 207.502 and 207.523). The state portion goes to the county treasurer inside a 15 day window that opens when the deed is handed over.

Run the numbers on $216,900, the median owner-occupied value QuickFacts reports for Eaton County. That divides into 434 steps. State tax comes to $1,627.50, county tax to $238.70, and the pair totals $1,866.20. A contract may shift the cost to the buyer at the table, though the statute still names the seller.

sections.h2: Which Eaton County deeds escape transfer tax?
sections.html:
Michigan exempts a long list of transfers, and the exemption has to be spelled out on the instrument. The county list is in MCL 207.505 and the state list in MCL 207.526. They share most entries, with one family difference noted below.

  • Consideration under $100.
  • Mortgages and other security instruments, plus their assignments and discharges.
  • Leases and leasehold transfers.
  • Court judgments and orders moving title with no stated price.
  • Quitclaim deeds that only repair a title defect.
  • Land contracts while legal title stays with the seller.
  • For the state tax only: a deed from a parent to a child or stepchild, or from a grandparent to a grandchild.

When tax was paid on a sale that should have qualified, MCL 207.523(4) allows the seller, or a buyer who paid for the seller, to request a refund from the state Department of Treasury.

sections.h2: How far back do Eaton County land records go online?
sections.html:
The search tool on the register's page covers every record from 1836 through the latest proof date, which makes a full chain of title possible from home. Beside it sits a link for e-recording.

Electronic filing helps sellers because a title company can submit the signed deed the same day without a courier. Ask your closer whether the file will go in electronically and when the recorded copy should reach you. Balances on a parcel are a separate question. The county treasurer runs its own parcel search for those.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about the Eaton County area?
sections.html:
Eaton County spans 579 square miles, 575 of them land, next to Ingham County and the city of Lansing, part of which lies inside Eaton. The state organized it on December 29, 1837 and named it for John H. Eaton, a secretary of war under President Jackson. Charlotte is the county seat. The other cities are Eaton Rapids, Grand Ledge, Olivet and Potterville.

Interstates 69, 96 and 496 run through the county, joined by M-43, M-50 and M-99. Eleven school districts serve it, among them Charlotte, Eaton Rapids, Grand Ledge, Olivet, Potterville, Maple Valley, Bellevue and Waverly, and a few edges send children to schools in neighboring counties. The road commission looks after more than 1,170 miles of county roads, most of them outside city limits.

  • QuickFacts puts the July 2025 population estimate at 109,581, with 48,090 housing units.
  • Owners live in 74.2% of homes. Emmet County, by comparison, is at 77.0%.
  • Typical household income is $79,597 across 45,428 households.
  • Rent runs a median $1,092 a month.

sections.h2: What if Eaton County taxes on the house are behind?
sections.html:
The county treasurer collects delinquent taxes and acts as the foreclosing unit for parcels that stay unpaid. The treasurer's page claims more than 2,000 foreclosures prevented since 2016 and links a chart of Michigan's statutory foreclosure deadlines.

Owners can pay delinquent bills online after looking up the parcel number and amount in the county's tax search. Cards carry a 2.49% fee, and parcels inside Lansing use a separate payment link. A county land bank takes on vacant and foreclosed property.

An owner in this spot can still sell. A payoff gets settled out of the sale money, and the treasurer's certificate tells the closer what has to clear first.

faqs.q: Where do I take a deed for recording in Eaton County?
faqs.a: To the Register of Deeds in Charlotte, the county seat. The register's page on eatoncounty.org gives the counter location, with weekday hours from 8:30 to 4:30 and a lunch closure from noon to 1:00.

faqs.q: What does Eaton County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars per document. An assignment or discharge covering several instruments adds $3 for each extra one, and a tax certificate runs $5 for up to 25 descriptions.

faqs.q: Can Eaton County take deeds electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. The register's page links an e-record option that title companies commonly use. Mailed paper filings must include a stamped return envelope addressed to the sender.

faqs.q: Does the seller or buyer owe Michigan transfer tax in Eaton County?
faqs.a: The seller, under the statutes. A purchase contract can hand the cost to the buyer, and the state share is remitted to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: How old are the land records Eaton County has online?
faqs.a: They begin in 1836. The search runs to the latest proof date, and the register's office can help with certified copies, which the website does not sell.
